one_line: the fresh reviewer calls loop 21 correct with caveats: the headline numbers recompute, identity and golden checks pass, TEST is untouched; but the vertex reduction is a re-count, one decision rule was bent, and several timing statements are above the load rule.
verdict: Correct with caveats. Every headline number recomputes from the stored files, the E260 identity and golden checks pass on a fresh run, no TEST split was used, and the one protected file that was edited had a decided grant (D20). The defects concern what the vertex number means, one decision rule that was relaxed after the sweep, and timing statements made on an overloaded machine.
rows: The stage lowers the node-id count (fast_recall 14.98 → 9.86, champion 14.83 → 9.52) but not the count on the basis of the 14.3 budget (per-piece Douglas-Peucker 0.3 m: 12.24 → 12.23 and 11.32 → 11.32; unique ends 8.37 / 8.07 unchanged). It re-counts the same geometry. Q is therefore unchanged by construction, and S rises only through its sparsity term.

The card demanded F1@0.5 loss ≤ 0.005 on both models; the champion loses 0.0053 at eps 0.3. decide.py returned KEEP on the pooled mean (the two models counted as seeds); eps 0.2 was then chosen after seeing the sweep. Disclosed in the summary, but a post-hoc choice.

Machine: 6 cores / 12 threads. E258 step 2 ran at load up to 9.1 and E259 at up to 15.2, above the rule; the E258 header says "3.5 - 4.2 during all timings" (false for step 2); "anchoring off saves 4.9 / 4.3 ms" matches the files only roughly (median 5.24 / 4.29). Used in the registry text and the HANDOVER as "about a fifth faster", "about 25 %", "~1 ms".

Its KEEP / CUT rule (identical graphs, saving ≥ 1.0 ms) was never run; step 1b is a different experiment; the J predictions (−0.01, −0.02) missed (−0.054, −0.004); no decide.py verdict; the per-family entry fast_recall_na is a post-hoc extension, and its J loss of 0.004 - 0.007 is consistently negative, so "free" overstates.

Prediction and rule were written into the run records before the runs started (E257.a0: 09:19:52, run 09:20:04); the cards were committed to git only afterwards, so the 1b amendment cannot be proven from git. E259.b0's prediction was written after E259.a0 finished.

E259 summary: Q +0.0016 should be +0.0015; the matched-budget argument is an extrapolation (E236 slope −0.005 per 0.5 vertices, E257 sweep −0.0044 per vertex); E257's secondary comparison pits the stage against the radius merge (not like-for-like); the HANDOVER header date and its "recall_dp entry" item are stale.

VAL 873 only in every run record; E257 numbers recomputed (vertices −5.99 / −6.31, Q −0.0008 / −0.0014); the registry names reproduce Q and vertices through evaluate.py; E258 and E259 tables match their files; the graph-hash baseline (22:56:58) pre-dates the code change (22:58:10) and all six hashes are identical on a fresh run; golden check reproduces 6 entries; 9 DP tests fail without the change; TEST log has no loop-21 entry; protected files untouched except PROBLEM.md under the D20 grant.
consequences: "One third fewer vertices" must be read as one third fewer nodes in the delivered graph (consumers that count nodes or edges gain), not as a better quality-per-vertex on the metric's own basis: there the graph is unchanged. Q cannot reveal a benefit of the stage, only the absence of a cost.
The Q numbers, the lanes-found / far-recall / J / topo-F1 gaps and the qualitative images are unaffected by the review.
Speed: the only speed numbers this report quotes are those of loop 18 (idle GPU) and E253 (idle); the loop-21 timing statements are treated as provisional and relative.

Records to correct (small, listed in the next steps): the PROBLEM.md sentence that compares a node-id count with the 14.3 budget (a protected file: needs a grant naming a decision), the E258 timing header, the E259 slips, the HANDOVER.
